arguments.value: This agreement amends a development agreement and a commercial license between Cargill and BioAmber. It lets Cargill temporarily add extra staff support in mid-2011 under the same payment terms as before. It also allows BioAmber to fund a Biotechnology Research Institute project and to carry out scale-up and production work, but only if those projects follow specific limits and eventually transition production to the CB1 biocatalyst. BioAmber must stop funding the research project once the re-engineered organism reaches a set production threshold, and any leftover funds must be used for something else. For the scale-up project, BioAmber must convert the Pomacle and Sarnia facilities to use CB1 and put in place agreements to make that possible. The commercial license is also amended to require BioAmber to use best efforts to get regulatory approvals for CB1 and to scale up CB1 fermentation, while keeping its broader obligation to replace the existing strains with CB1 at current and future facilities.
